source_locator.description: Gunasekaran reaches Tiruchi after failing to find Kalyani in Madurai, takes Vimala's luggage as if for hire, runs, and escapes with only the food when chased.

notes: The source contains a nested parenthetical ending with `தன் பசியின் கொடுமையை அறிந்து`; the English preserves it as a separate bracketed thought rather than inventing a completed action.
translation.english_text: (After failing to find Kalyani in Madurai, Gunasekaran reaches Tiruchi and is near the railway station. At that moment he takes the luggage of a woman named Vimala, who has arrived by train, saying he will carry it for hire, and runs away. When some people chase him, he takes only the food and runs. [Aware of the cruelty of his hunger.])

source_locator.description: Gunasekaran sits by the well in the rear garden of Vimala's house, eating the stolen food and singing.

translation.english_text: (The man who stole the food sits by the well in the rear garden of Vimala's house, eating it as he sings.)

notes: This is the verified soundtrack occurrence `parasakthi-song-008`; its PDF 31→32 boundary is preserved as one translation unit.

The source forms `பட்டி சாதி` and `பட்சமாயிருங்க` are textually verified but semantically pressure-sensitive in this context. They are provisionally transliterated in English rather than silently repaired; the second pass should revisit them without changing Tamil.
english_lines: Kaa—kaa—kaa—kaa—
To eat, everyone gather as one;
come running with affection—
to make the lesson of experience clear, O crow-brothers,
with your lovely mouths
you sing a melody—crying kaa, kaa,
you gather together as one—come. (Kaa)
People are suffering without food;
they cry aloud, their hearts in anguish;
when they ask, 'Pour us some gruel-water to save a life,'
look—you bolt the doors.
Where are those cruel ones? Let selfishness leave;
sing that raga upon the earth. (Kaa)
For rice thrown among spit-stained leavings,
beggars fight—on the road;
the weak and the strong,
communal quarrels, money quarrels—
how many in this country.
Let `patti saathi` go—
do not look for our rationalists;
be `patcham`, live by sharing what you eat;
do not change that habit—come, sing. (Kaa)

source_locator.description: Vimala is drawn by the song, comes there, and Gunasekaran runs away in fear; she gives him the title Puthumaippithan.

notes: `புதுமைப்பித்தன்` is retained as the source's Tamil title/name rather than replaced with an external literary reference.
translation.english_text: (Drawn there by the charm of the song, Vimala comes over. Seeing her, Gunasekaran runs away in fear. She bestows on him the title 'Puthumaippithan'.)
